chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd ibn al-Ahwas, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in the skins of predatory animals, and he said: “Do not pray in them.”
He said: And I asked him whether a man may pray in a garment of silk, and he said: “No.”

key_terms.إِبْرِيسَمٍ: silk, referring here to a silk garment
key_terms.السِّبَاعِ: predatory animals whose skins are mentioned as impermissible for prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.ثَوْبِ: garment or clothing worn by a person
key_terms.جُلُودِ: skins or hides used as clothing or material

ai.seo_question: Can a man perform salat (prayer) in the skin of predatory animals or in a silk garment?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding what may not be worn in salat (prayer). It states that salat (prayer) is not to be performed in the skins of predatory animals nor in a silk garment by a man, indicating restrictions on prayer attire in fiqh.
